title: A Fully Constructive Transcendental Gδ — Explicit Decreasing Dense-Open Sequence
description: Upgrades the parent's abstract dense-Gδ witness for the transcendental reals to a fully constructive one. The parent proves the transcendentals are a dense Gδ only via IsGδ.biInter_of_isOpen over the family of singleton complements {a}ᶜ — it never hands you an honest sequence you could enumerate. This entry fixes an explicit enumeration algEnum : ℕ → ℝ of the (countable, nonempty) algebraic reals and defines U n = (algEnum '' Set.Iic n)ᶜ — the reals with the first n+1 enumerated algebraics removed. Each U n is open (complement of a finite, hence closed, set), dense (complement of a countable set in the perfect Baire space ℝ), and the sequence is decreasing (Antitone). The headline iInter_U proves ⋂ n, U n is EXACTLY the transcendentals {x | ¬ IsAlgebraic ℚ x}: stage k removes algEnum k and nothing else is removed. The Gδ property is then re-derived directly from the explicit open sequence via IsGδ.iInter_of_isOpen, answering the parent OQ01's own second open question (a constructive enumeration of the algebraic reals and the resulting monotone sequence) on the Gδ side.

overview.historicalContext: The transcendental reals are a textbook example of a comeagre (residual) set: Cantor's 1874 countability argument shows the algebraic numbers are countable, hence the transcendentals are an uncountable dense Gδ in $\mathbb{R}$. The framing as a dense Gδ belongs to the Baire-category theory developed by René Baire (1899) and popularized by Oxtoby's *Measure and Category* (Springer GTM 2) and Kechris's *Classical Descriptive Set Theory* (Springer GTM 156). The standard classroom proof writes the transcendentals as $\bigcap_a \{a\}^c$ over all algebraic $a$, an intersection indexed by an abstract countable set rather than by an honest sequence $\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}$. Baire-category arguments, however, are applied to *sequences* of dense open sets, so the constructive form — an explicit decreasing sequence — is the version actually used in practice. This entry supplies that sequence, completing the parent's abstract witness and the constructive open question recorded by the sibling $F_\sigma$ entry.
overview.problemStatement: The parent entry proves the transcendentals $\{x \in \mathbb{R} \mid \neg\,\mathrm{IsAlgebraic}_\mathbb{Q}\,x\}$ are a dense $G_\delta$ only abstractly, via $\mathrm{IsG\delta.biInter\_of\_isOpen}$ over the family of singleton complements $\{a\}^c$ for all algebraic $a$, never producing an enumerable sequence. The task is to exhibit a fully constructive witness: an explicit enumeration $\mathrm{algEnum}:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}$ of the algebraic reals and a decreasing sequence of dense open sets $U_n = (\mathrm{algEnum}\,''\,\mathrm{Set.Iic}\,n)^c$ such that each $U_n$ is open, each $U_n$ is dense, $U$ is antitone, and $\bigcap_n U_n = \{x \mid \neg\,\mathrm{IsAlgebraic}_\mathbb{Q}\,x\}$ exactly, with the $G_\delta$ property re-derived from this sequence.
overview.proofStrategy: Fix an enumeration $\mathrm{algEnum}:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}$ whose range is exactly the algebraic reals — they are countable ($\mathrm{algebraic\_reals\_countable}$) and nonempty ($0$ is algebraic), so $\mathrm{Set.Countable.exists\_eq\_range}$ yields such a sequence. Define $U_n = (\mathrm{algEnum}\,''\,\mathrm{Set.Iic}\,n)^c$, the reals with the first $n+1$ enumerated algebraics removed. Each removed set is finite ($\mathrm{Set.finite\_Iic}$ image), hence closed in the $T_1$ space $\mathbb{R}$, so $U_n$ is open; and dense because $\mathbb{R}$ is a perfect Baire space where the complement of any countable set is dense (the parent's $\mathrm{dense\_compl\_of\_countable}$). Since $\mathrm{Set.Iic}\,n$ grows with $n$, the removed sets grow and the $U_n$ shrink (Antitone). The headline $\mathrm{iInter\_U}$ computes the intersection: $\bigcup_n \mathrm{algEnum}\,''\,\mathrm{Iic}\,n$ collapses via $\mathrm{Set.image\_iUnion}$ and $\bigcup_n \mathrm{Iic}\,n = \mathrm{univ}$ to the full range of $\mathrm{algEnum}$, i.e. the algebraic reals; De Morgan ($\mathrm{Set.compl\_iUnion}$) then gives $\bigcap_n U_n = \{x \mid \neg\,\mathrm{IsAlgebraic}_\mathbb{Q}\,x\}$. Finally $\mathrm{IsG\delta.iInter\_of\_isOpen}$ applied to the explicit open sequence re-derives the $G_\delta$ property, and everything is packaged into one constructive statement.
keyInsights: Replacing the abstract $\mathrm{biInter}$ over the family of all algebraic singleton complements with a concrete sequence $U:\mathbb{N}\to\mathrm{Set}\,\mathbb{R}$ is what makes the witness usable: Baire-category theorems are stated for sequences of dense open sets, not for arbitrary countable families.

An enumeration of the algebraic reals exists because they are both countable and nonempty; $\mathrm{Set.Countable.exists\_eq\_range}$ needs the nonemptiness witness, supplied by $0$ being algebraic ($\mathrm{isAlgebraic\_zero}$).

$U_n = (\mathrm{algEnum}\,''\,\mathrm{Set.Iic}\,n)^c$ removes only a finite set at each stage, so openness follows from finite sets being closed in the $T_1$ space $\mathbb{R}$ ($\mathrm{Set.Finite.isClosed}$), while density reuses the parent's perfect-Baire-space lemma for complements of countable sets.

Monotonicity is purely order-theoretic: $\mathrm{Set.Iic}$ is monotone in $n$, so the removed images grow and complementation reverses inclusion, yielding $\mathrm{Antitone}\,U$ — exactly the decreasing structure a Baire argument consumes.

The intersection identity is the heart of the proof: every algebraic real $\mathrm{algEnum}\,k$ is removed precisely at stage $k$ and nothing transcendental is ever removed, so $\bigcap_n U_n$ is the transcendentals exactly — established by collapsing $\bigcup_n \mathrm{Iic}\,n$ to $\mathrm{univ}$ and applying De Morgan.

The construction is choice-bounded but explicit: only $\mathrm{algEnum}$ uses $\mathrm{Classical.choice}$ (via $\mathrm{exists\_eq\_range}$); the sequence $U_n$ and all its properties are then derived with the standard Mathlib triple of axioms, leaving open the question of a fully computable recursive enumeration of algebraic roots.

conclusion.summary: A 128-line, 0-sorry, 0-axiom formalization upgrading the parent's abstract dense-Gδ witness for the transcendental reals to a fully constructive one: an explicit enumeration algEnum of the algebraic reals and a decreasing sequence U n = (algEnum '' Iic n)ᶜ of dense open sets whose intersection is exactly the transcendentals. The Gδ property is re-derived from the explicit sequence via IsGδ.iInter_of_isOpen.
conclusion.implications: Where the parent only certified existence of a dense Gδ structure, this entry exhibits a concrete antitone basis for it. The decreasing dense-open sequence is the form actually used in Baire-category arguments (one applies the Baire theorem to a sequence, not to an uncountable family), so the result turns the parent's classification into something directly usable. It also closes the constructive open question raised by the sibling Fσ entry on the Gδ side: the Fσ entry asks for an increasing sequence of finite closed sets ⋃_{k≤n}{a k}; here the complementary decreasing sequence of dense open sets is built and its intersection identified.
openQuestions: Make the enumeration itself computable: replace the Classical.choice-extracted algEnum with an explicit recursive enumeration of algebraic reals (e.g. by diagonalizing over integer polynomials and their real roots) so that U n becomes a decidable/computable sequence and the whole construction is choice-free.

Quantify the approximation: for a fixed transcendental x, bound the rate at which the dense open sets U n shrink around x, relating the construction to effective transcendence measures (e.g. Liouville-type lower bounds on |x − algEnum k|).

sections.summary: Module docstring. States the parent's second open question — its transcendental dense-Gδ witness is only abstract (via IsGδ.biInter_of_isOpen over the family {a}ᶜ), with no honest sequence to enumerate; can this be made fully constructive? Answers by fixing an enumeration algEnum : ℕ → ℝ of the algebraic reals and defining Uₙ = (algEnum '' Iic n)ᶜ, each open (finite complement), dense (countable complement in a perfect Baire space), decreasing, with ⋂ₙ Uₙ exactly the transcendentals — upgrading the abstract Gδ witness to a concrete antitone basis. Lists the eight declared results.
sections.mathContext: Being told a set is $G_\delta$ via `IsGδ.biInter_of_isOpen` over an arbitrary countable index gives no canonical enumeration; fixing a bijection $\mathrm{algEnum} : \mathbb{N} \to \{\text{algebraic reals}\}$ and removing one more point per stage, $U_n = (\mathrm{algEnum}(\{0,\dots,n\}))^c$, produces an explicit antitone dense-open sequence with $\bigcap_n U_n$ exactly the transcendentals.
